newsitem.title: USA: CME 3-month T-bill contracts to be cash-settled.
newsitem.headline: CME 3-month T-bill contracts to be cash-settled.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said Wednesday its three-month Treasury bill futures and options will move to cash settlement from the current physical delivery settlement system.
The CME will list cash-settled December 1997 and March 1998 contracts on Monday, and all new three-month T-bill contracts will be cash-settled, CME said in a statement.

October contracts, the first serial-month expiration for T-bills, will be listed in July, and all-or-none (AON) trading with a minimum threshold of 100 contracts will be applied for the new cash-settled contracts.
It said the Commodity Futures Trading Commission approved the changes today.

Cash settlement would improve the liquidity of CME's T-bill contracts and make it easier to transact TED (Treasury/Eurodollar) spreads, promoting the use of both T-bill futures and Eurodollar futures, the exchange said.
